units.passage: Los procesos de investigación están regulados por los organismos dispuestos
units.policy: Research processes are regulated by University bodies and by the agencies that sponsor the research.
units.why: It says research processes "están regulados por los organismos dispuestos en la Universidad y por las agencias que auspician"; defers to institutional and funder rules, P62.

units.passage: The academic integrity policy applies to all students, undergraduate and graduate, and to scholarly pursuits and research.
units.why: The policy says 'The academic integrity policy applies to all students, undergraduate and graduate, and to scholarly pursuits and research', which sets scope; with the AI sentence it covers AI in research too. P62 is nearest but fits only partly.
units.fit_note: A general scope of the integrity policy to research; does not mention AI in research or defer to venue rules.

units.passage: Consult with your department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research, particularly for handling sensitive or proprietary data
units.policy: Researchers consult with their department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research, particularly for handling sensitive or proprietary data
units.why: "Consult with your department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research" sets research AI duties and defers to department and regulations; P62. The Researchers guideline has no actor value of its own, so actor all; should as an Additional Guideline.

units.passage: AI use in Research, including the development of AI and other machine learning, must be conducted in accordance with applicable policies and governing Research
units.policy: AI use in Research, including the development of AI and other machine learning, must be conducted in accordance with applicable policies
units.why: "AI use in Research ... must be conducted in accordance with applicable policies and governing Research" defers research AI to existing research rules, which is P62.

units.passage: AI also plays a crucial role in research and knowledge discovery. Faculty can utilize AI algorithms to analyze vast amounts of data, identify trends, and generate insights that would otherwise be challenging to uncover manually. AI can assist in literature reviews, data analysis, and experimental design, leading to more rigorous and impactful research outcomes.
units.why: 'AI can assist in literature reviews, data analysis, and experimental design'; AI in research, P62.
units.fit_note: Encourages AI in research work; no governance rules.

units.passage: Researchers utilizing AI must comply with all applicable federal regulations, agency guidance, sponsor requirements, contractual obligations, and University policies governing the conduct of research (including research misconduct ) and use of artificial intelligence. This includes adherence to restrictions, prohibitions, disclosure requirements, data security standards, export control regulations, human subjects protections, and other research compliance requirements that may limit or govern the use of specific AI tools or platforms.
units.why: Researchers "must comply with all applicable federal regulations, agency guidance, sponsor requirements" and university policy; AI rules for research that defer to funders and regulators are P62.

units.passage: Be transparent regarding AI use in research, including describing methods, acknowledgements, or elsewhere, as appropriate.
units.why: "Be transparent regarding AI use in research, including describing methods, acknowledgements" requires research disclosure; P62 because the setting is research, not coursework.

units.passage: AI-generated research output must be clearly identified, and authorship must reflect substantive human contributions. Researchers must comply with the terms of any federal, state or private grants with regards to AI use or allowability, as well as any written policies outlined by scientific or other journals where research output is published.
units.why: 'authorship must reflect substantive human contributions' limits AI authorship in research outputs, P62.

units.passage: AI-generated research output must be clearly identified, and authorship must reflect substantive human contributions. Researchers must comply with the terms of any federal, state or private grants with regards to AI use or allowability, as well as any written policies outlined by scientific or other journals where research output is published.
units.policy: Authorship of research that uses AI must reflect substantive human contributions.
units.why: The same sentence also states that 'authorship must reflect substantive human contributions', a separate rule on authorship, so it is its own unit under P62 (research use), must, with the research context in 'AI-generated research output'.

units.passage: Researchers are responsible for the accuracy of any content created by AI that is included in any research output. Use caution, as AI has been known to generate non-existent citations or images for experiments that were never conducted.
units.why: 'Researchers are responsible for the accuracy of any content created by AI' warns about fabricated citations, a research-scholarship accuracy rule, P62.
units.fit_note: Accuracy duty specific to research output.

units.passage: Avoid uploading or using as input any unpublished research data, including data provided by or pertaining to researchers or research subjects into generative AI tools. Doing so may lead to the disclosure of unpublished work, impede future intellectual property protection, or create privacy violations. This includes unpublished manuscripts or funding proposals that researchers may be asked to peer review, as some funding agencies (e.g., NIH, NSF) prohibit using generative AI for peer review.
units.why: 'Avoid uploading or using as input any unpublished research data' limits inputs in research and peer review, P62.
units.fit_note: Also protects data and IP, closer to P50 but specific to research and peer review.

units.passage: This includes unpublished manuscripts or funding proposals that researchers may be asked to peer review, as some funding agencies (e.g., NIH, NSF) prohibit using generative AI for peer review.
units.why: "some funding agencies (e.g., NIH, NSF) prohibit using generative AI for peer review" is a fact about funder rules on AI in peer review, P62.

units.passage: Researchers are expected to follow the policies of journals, funding agencies, and professional societies through which they report their research (e.g., some journals explicitly prohibit AI-generated text, figures, images, or graphics).
units.why: "Researchers are expected to follow the policies of journals, funding agencies, and professional societies" defers AI rules to venues and funders, P62.

units.passage: The application of AI in sensitive research areas (e.g., biomedical, social sciences) may require Institutional Review Board (IRB) or other research compliance committee approvals, as applicable. Please refer to the Institutional Review Board standard operating policies and procedures for the protection of human research subjects policy in PolicyStat for more information.
units.why: "may require Institutional Review Board (IRB) or other research compliance committee approvals" sets IRB review for AI in sensitive research, P62.

units.passage: Researchers should confirm that the selected tool is approved for the data involved and consult the appropriate research or compliance office when a proposed use is unclear.
units.why: "Researchers should confirm that the selected tool is approved for the data involved and consult the appropriate research or compliance office" is a research-specific duty to check tool approval; P62 fits as research use. Consensus codes: actor=all, phase=during-work, modality=should, policy_type=P62, unit_stance=neutral.
units.fit_note: Researchers include faculty and students; also directs them to compliance offices.

units.passage: The use of AI in research remains subject to applicable requirements related to: Human subjects and Institutional Review Board review Privacy and informed consent Research-data classification and security Sponsor, grant, and contractual restrictions Intellectual property and publication Attribution, authorship, and reproducibility
units.why: "The use of AI in research remains subject to applicable requirements related to" IRB, privacy, sponsors and IP governs AI in research and scholarship, P62.

units.passage: Research remains subject to applicable institutional, sponsor, privacy, and compliance requirements.
units.why: "Research remains subject to applicable institutional, sponsor, privacy, and compliance requirements" defers research AI use to sponsor and compliance rules, which is the P62 definition.

units.passage: Researchers are responsible for the accuracy of any content created by AI that is included in any research output and should use caution in utilizing AI output in research.
units.why: 'Researchers are responsible for the accuracy of any content created by AI' in research outputs; research accountability, P62.
units.fit_note: A research-specific accountability rule; P29 and P31 cover student work.

units.passage: Researchers are expected to follow the policies of journals, funding agencies and professional societies through which they report their research.
units.why: Researchers 'are expected to follow the policies of journals, funding agencies and professional societies'; deferring to venue and funder rules, P62.

units.passage: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) and U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), among others, prohibit using AI tools for peer review.
units.why: Says NIH and NSF 'prohibit using AI tools for peer review'; a research rule for peer review, P62.

units.passage: Researchers should comply with the expectations of their respective school, department and sub-discipline, as well as journal and/or publisher requirements, as applicable, which may include documenting AI tools' role in research, including but not limited to:
units.why: Researchers 'should comply with the expectations of their respective school, department and sub-discipline'; defers to unit and venue rules for research, P62.

units.passage: Seattle University supports academic research to create and improve artificial intelligence (AI) systems in line with its Principles for Safe, Fair and Accountable AI Development and Use. It encourages research about the moral, legal, business, social, political, economic, military, and cultural aspects of AI development and use. Such research includes, but is not limited to, foundational research to understand and explain AI systems, the use of AI tools in academic research and scholarship, use of AI in teaching and learning, assessment of AI tools' effectiveness, legality and conformity to ethical standards, and policy and governance research.
units.why: The research section says the university 'supports academic research to create and improve artificial intelligence (AI) systems' and 'encourages research about the moral, legal' aspects of AI, a research-scope statement; P62 fits.

units.passage: However, the misuse of AI in research threatens to deepen the crisis of research integrity, as opportunities for plagiarism, data fabrication, and misinformation increase significantly.
units.why: 'The misuse of AI in research threatens to deepen the crisis of research integrity' as plagiarism, fabrication and misinformation rise, giving a reason for research rules; P62 fits.

units.passage: All AI-producing and AI-using research should conform to the University's academic integrity policy and Institutional Review Board expectations.
units.why: 'All AI-producing and AI-using research should conform to the University's academic integrity policy and Institutional Review Board expectations' ties research to existing rules and IRB review; P62 fits (P77 also applies, but the research focus is the better home).
units.fit_note: Also ties research to the university integrity policy (P77 content).

units.passage: AI tools may be used for identifying relevant literature and citations, but human oversight should accompany this process, as reliance on AI tools to generate citations may be error-prone – and in some cases, outright non-existent.
units.why: 'AI tools may be used for identifying relevant literature and citations, but human oversight this process', permitting AI literature search with human oversight; P62 fits.

units.passage: In fields where original real-world data collection is necessary, the use of AI-generated data amounts to fabrication, and therefore, a violation of academic integrity.
units.why: 'The use of AI-generated data amounts to fabrication, and therefore, a violation of academic integrity' where real-world data collection is needed, banning AI-made data; P62 fits.

units.passage: Academic researchers should refrain from using AI-generated output as data in all but exceptional cases.
units.why: "Academic researchers should refrain from using AI-generated output as data in all but exceptional cases" restricts AI-generated data in research (P62).

units.passage: When computer-generated data may be legitimately used, the data generation process should be acknowledged.
units.why: 'When computer-generated data may be legitimately used, the data generation process should be acknowledged' sets disclosure for synthetic data; P62 fits.

units.passage: academic researchers should acknowledge their use of AI-powered data analysis and always check for accuracy and reliability.
units.why: Researchers 'should acknowledge their use of AI-powered data analysis and always check for accuracy and reliability', combining disclosure and checking in research; P62 fits.

units.passage: AI tools should be seen as facilitators, rather than decision-makers, in data analysis.
units.why: 'AI tools should be seen as facilitators, rather than decision-makers, in data analysis' keeps the researcher as decider; P62 chosen over P32 because the context is research methodology.
units.fit_note: Equivalent to P32 (keep humans in charge), applied to research analysis.

units.passage: In addition, researchers should conform to the submission rules of the journals, publishing presses, and other platforms while communicating research results.
units.why: 'Researchers should conform to the submission rules of the journals, publishing presses, and other platforms' defers to venue rules; P62 fits.

units.passage: Thus, human subjects ethics review should incorporate a component of data privacy and protection vis-à-vis AI tools.
units.why: 'Human subjects ethics review should incorporate a component of data privacy and protection vis-à-vis AI tools' adds AI privacy to IRB review; P62 fits.

units.passage: research projects that use algorithms or AI-generated output in conformity with academic integrity standards should fully disclose their use of AI.
units.why: Projects using AI output 'should fully disclose their use of AI', a research disclosure rule; P62 chosen over P24 because it is limited to research projects.
units.fit_note: Research-project disclosure for replicability.

units.passage: Never use public Generative AI tools to train AI models for people/human subjects unless those individuals have explicitly agreed to such usage and that the use of the data complies with SMU policies
units.why: Bars using public AI 'to train AI models for people/human subjects' without explicit agreement; a research-ethics condition, coded P62.
units.fit_note: Concerns training models on human-subject data and consent, partly outside research and scholarship as such (theses, manuscripts, grants).

units.passage: These guidelines apply to public cloud-hosted Generative AI tools, Generative AI tools or AI models hosted by SMU researchers will provide their own security disclaimers and should be appropriately developed with SMU’s IRB’s policies.
units.why: The page says AI tools or models hosted by SMU researchers 'should be appropriately developed with SMU's IRB's policies', which makes research AI development follow IRB policy. The addressee is researchers, who are not a separate actor value, so all; P62 governs AI in research, modality should, phase general.

units.policy: The policy does not provide guidance for GenAI use in graduate thesis and dissertation work or in overall research processes; a separate policy will cover thesis and dissertation work

A separate policy will cover thesis and dissertation work". It sets scope and informs, addresses all, and falls under P62 (govern AI use in research and scholarship).

units.why: Research guidance comes from the Office of Sponsored Projects and 'should also follow specific agency grant and contract guidelines and/or specific publisher allowances', deferring to funders and publishers: P62.

units.why: They "should document methodology, data sources, and algorithms" in AI research, a documentation duty in research, P62.

units.why: "Ensure that AI research complies with institutional review board (IRB) protocols, ethical standards, and sponsor imposed contractual requirements" defers to IRB and sponsor rules, so P62, must.

units.passage: Similarly, ChatGPT or similar AI Tools must not be used to generate output that would be considered non-public. units.policy: AI Tools must not be used to generate non-public output such as proprietary or unpublished research.
units.why: "generating proprietary or unpublished research" is listed as prohibited output, an AI rule for research and scholarship, P62.

units.passage: Authors are responsible for checking the accuracy of the AI-generated outputs and should carefully edit any incorrect, incomplete, or biased content.

units.passage: Research Considerations with Generative AI Developing manuscripts and grant applications using AI : ▪ Authors must be transparent to the journal and the paper's co-authors in disclosing the use of generative AI tools for creating any portion of the work. ▪ Authors are responsible for checking the accuracy of the AI-generated outputs and should carefully edit any incorrect, incomplete, or biased content. ▪ Generative AI can help create outlines or summaries within the limitations described in the two above points. ▪ The use of generative AI tools for writing manuscripts or grant proposals may be prohibited in many cases. Check the specific journal or grant application requirements before using any AI tool. ▪ Never upload your grant application (novel idea) into any AI tool as then it will be in the public domain and accessible by others. AI and Peer Reviews Researchers should always check with the sponsoring agency regarding their policies and normal expectations for preparing reviews.
units.why: "Generative AI can help create outlines or summaries" permits a research use within limits, so P62.

units.passage: The use of generative AI tools for writing manuscripts or grant proposals may be prohibited in many cases. Check the specific journal or grant application requirements before using any AI tool

units.passage: Never upload your grant application (novel idea) into any AI tool as then it will be in the public domain and accessible by others.

units.passage: Researchers should always check with the sponsoring agency regarding their policies and normal expectations for preparing reviews

units.passage: Do not let AI become a source of research misconduct. Fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism, whether produced by you or by an AI tool you used, can constitute research misconduct under federal definitions, and a number of federal agencies now explicitly treat AI-induced FFP as misconduct. You are responsible for the integrity of anything you propose, perform, review, submit, publish, or attribute to yourself.
units.why: 'Do not let AI become a source of research misconduct' with fabrication, falsification, plagiarism treated as misconduct: a research-integrity rule, P62 (AI in research and scholarship).

units.passage: The AI for Research subgroup develops research-specific guidance, creates intellectual property guidelines for AI-generated research outputs, and establishes publication standards and data handling protocols for AI-assisted research.

units.passage: This revision must systematically address patent and copyright implications for AI-assisted research while protecting both institutional and individual researcher interests. The Policy on Misconduct in Research (Policy 13020) would benefit from establishment of supporting citation standards for large language model usage (see Appendix B: Research - Detailed Policy Assessment, Section B.2.3) and disclosure requirements that maintain research integrity and transparency.
units.why: The research misconduct policy needs 'supporting citation standards for large language model usage' and disclosure requirements (P62).

units.passage: he practical implementation guide provides data handling decision trees that guide appropriate AI tool usage in research contexts, establishes publication standards and attribution requirements for AI-generated content that maintain scholarly integrity (addressing gaps identified in Appendix B.2.3: Research policies, specifically Policies 13000 and 13020), and develops intellectual property guidelines that protect both institutional and researcher interests in AI-enhanced research outputs.
units.why: The Research guide will provide 'data handling decision trees that guide appropriate AI tool usage in research contexts' (P62).

units.passage: Faculty have identified critical gaps in current guidance regarding AI use in dissertations, theses, and examinations (see Appendix B.2.2: Academic Affairs policy analysis) — contexts where original thought and independent scholarship are paramount.
units.why: 'Faculty have identified critical gaps in current guidance regarding AI use in dissertations, theses, and examinations': research scholarship rules are missing (P62).
units.fit_note: Also names examinations, an assessment context. | Also names examinations, which P62 does not cover.

units.passage: It is important to provide faculty with training and instructions on how to use AI in research projects, and how to most effectively document how it is being used
units.why: 'It is important to provide faculty with training and instructions on how to use AI in research projects' calls for research-use guidance, P62.

units.passage: Any such training must at minimum address how the use of AI in research must be documented and made transparent
units.why: 'any such training must at minimum address how the use of AI in research must be documented and made transparent' requires documenting AI in research (P62); admin, before-course, must.

units.passage: Ethics in research are paramount to faculty research. The Provost should task the Vice Provost of Research to address these issues as follows: • Develop resources for faculty/researchers on acceptable use practices. • Work in consultation with the CIO to identify acceptable AI tools for faculty and students to use in their research. • Developing a public-facing framework on the ethical and responsible use of AI in research. • Provide training and development for faculty, researchers, and students on the acceptable use of AI in research.
units.why: The VPR should 'Develop resources for faculty/researchers on acceptable use practices' for AI in research (P62); admin, before-course, should.

units.passage: Developing a public-facing framework on the ethical and responsible use of AI in research.
units.why: 'Developing a public-facing framework on the ethical and responsible use of AI in research' sets a research-use framework, P62.

units.passage: Training on use of AI in research extends from data collection to analysis to writing. Proper citation when using AI is a requirement for all AI assisted research. Finally, the use of GenAI to improve operational efficiencies should occur.
units.why: 'Proper citation when using AI is a requirement for all AI assisted research' sets a citation duty in research (P62); all, during-work, must.

units.passage: Four issues were listed as central to regulating the use of AI for research: • Transparency—documentation of use of AI in research design and reporting • Ethical oversight—institutional review boards or AI ethics committees • Faculty autonomy with guardrails—encouraging innovation while ensuring accountability • Education and training—equipping faculty with the skills to use AI responsibly This section focuses on three areas of AI use in research that require attention as William & Mary codifies policies and practices for the ethical use of AI in research.
units.why: Four issues listed as central to regulating AI in research, starting 'Transparency-documentation of use of AI in research design and reporting' (P62); all, general, informs.

units.passage: Adopt shared standards and tools for evaluating AI reliability, reproducibility, transparency, and uncertainty quantification, especially in federally funded or high - stakes domains such as healthcare, climate science, and national security. 3.
units.why: 'Adopt shared standards and tools for evaluating AI reliability, reproducibility, transparency, and uncertainty quantification' sets research standards, P62.

units.passage: The methodology for producing and validating the fidelity of a synthetic dataset must be clearly documented and be reproducible in the publication
units.why: 'The methodology for producing and validating the fidelity of a synthetic dataset must be clearly documented and be reproducible in the publication' is a research AI rule (P62); all, during-work, must.

units.passage: Processes for human review should be included in data analysis and in data accuracy
units.why: 'Processes for human review should be included in data analysis and in data accuracy' keeps humans in research analysis, P62.
units.fit_note: Concerns human review of data analysis in research, not decisions about individuals.

units.passage: AI tools should be evaluated for reliability prior to using them regularly in research
units.why: 'AI tools should be evaluated for reliability prior to using them regularly in research' sets a tool check for research, P62.

units.passage: AI tools should be evaluated for reliability prior to using them regularly in research. REPORTING OF AI USAGE IN RESEARCH Researchers must clearly disclose the use of generative AI tools in all research outputs. Such disclosures must include the exact AI tool utilized (e.g., Chat GPT, Deep Research) along with its version.
units.why: 'Researchers must clearly disclose the use of generative AI tools in all research outputs' is a research disclosure rule (P62); all, during-work, must.
units.fit_note: A disclosure rule (P24-like) that applies to researchers, not student coursework.

units.passage: They argue that citation of AI use by faculty should be mandatory when an AI tool makes decisions that could affect research results, when AI analyzes content or data (e.g., qualitative coding of transcripts), or when AI generates manuscript materials (e.g., visuals, data, content) (p. 1)
units.why: 'citation of AI use by faculty should be mandatory when an AI tool makes decisions that could affect research results' reports a framework recommending mandatory citation (P62); informs.

units.passage: At minimum, researchers should acknowledge the use of AI tools explicitly, either within the acknowledgments section or in supplementary materials accompanying the main publication
units.why: 'researchers should acknowledge the use of AI tools explicitly, either within the acknowledgments section or in supplementary materials' (P62); all, during-work, should.

units.passage: To maintain clarity and consistency, academic departments and schools are advised to create and distribute standardized templates for acknowledging AI contributions
units.why: 'academic departments and schools are advised to create and distribute standardized templates for acknowledging AI contributions' asks units to supply disclosure templates, P62.

units.passage: Provide centralized resources to guide faculty and students on ways to cite the use of AI in their publications and papers
units.why: 'Provide centralized resources to guide faculty and students on ways to cite the use of AI in their publications and papers' (P62); admin, before-course, should.

units.passage: Material under confidential review, including research papers and funding proposals
units.policy: Material under confidential review, including research papers and funding proposals, may not be entered into a generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review.
units.why: 'Material under confidential review, including research papers and funding proposals' may not be entered into AI tools, a research-confidentiality rule (P62).
units.fit_note: A data-entry ban on confidential research materials, not a general rule for AI in research.
